description: The corpus's 3-body cumulant is exactly minus the classical third Ursell function under the Boltzmann identification g = f - 1. The classical Ursell functions ALTERNATE in the repulsive class, (-1)^(n-1) phi^T_n >= 0, while the corpus carries a uniform minus at n=2 and n=3. The uniform minus is correct at n=2 and inverts the physical sign at n=3, so MayerThreeBodySign's b3 < 0 is a missing (-1)^(n-1) rather than a physical obstruction. The identity is low-order: it does not extend to n=4 under either sign.
convention: D (z = q^3/(q^2+1)), canonical per owner ruling R1 2026-08-15

assertions.name: corpus b3 == -phi^T_3 exactly, on every random non-uniform triple
mu is the Boltzmann factor of the Sec.10a bond energy: mu in (0,1), v = B/alpha > 0, and e^-v == mu, in BOTH conventions
the identity does NOT extend to n=4 under either sign
(-1)^(n-1) phi^T_n >= 0 holds for every n and trial in the repulsive class
the OCR'd (-1)^n law FAILS at n=2, which is how the exponent is settled
at both typings the corpus b3 is negative and phi^T_3 is positive
restoring the alternation gives b3 > 0, the sign AME has

scope: (a). Does NOT refute MayerThreeBodySign -- every statement there remains true of the object it is about. What is established is that that object differs from the classical one by a sign the classical theory does not carry. The Boltzmann identification f = e^{-v} IS derived, by the corpus's own Sec.10a log form read backwards (see boltzmann_chain). What is NOT fixed here is the normalisation of the cluster expansion's n-body term: the sign is settled, the magnitude is reported under two scale conventions differing by ~10%.
source: Jansen & Kolesnikov, J. Stat. Phys. 189:33 (2022), library/s10955-022-02992-6/ -- definitions on p.5, sign property in section 3.1. The OCR of Eq. (3.1) reads (-1)^n and is inconsistent with the paper's own Corollary 3.3; settled here by computation from the definitions, not from the scanned superscript.
